text:
miguel: hey team — following up on the scheduler convo. idea: move from fixed coalesce windows to a variance-aware window that adapts per-tenant request variance. goal is to cut 99.9% tail for mixed short/long requests without hurting median.
sara: tl;dr? how do we detect "variance" cheaply at admission?
miguel: simple sketch: maintain exponentially weighted variance of token length and observed decode time per client id. use that to pick target window size and max-wait. cheap counters + a couple of uint32s per tenant.
jen: sounds ok but worried about oscillation when load shifts fast (flash sales). how do we avoid thrashing windows and extra evictions?
miguel: add hysteresis: only change window if metric crosses threshold for N consecutive windows, and clamp change rate. also fallback to global defaults on sudden load spikes.
kevin: curious about fairness — won't high-variance tenants start hogging batch slots because they stretch windows?
miguel: we keep a per-tenant admission credit and a soft cap on concurrent inflight batches. variance increases window but doesn't grant extra concurrency. if tenant tries to exceed credit it gets queued on normal priority.
oliver: could we leverage sampling to avoid per-tenant state explosion? e.g., maintain variance at tenant-group or model-route granularity?
miguel: yes, route-granularity helps. default to route-level, backfill tenant-level for flagged customers.
sara: observability reqs? ops needs to see when windows change and why, otherwise debugging tails will be hell.
jen: +1. we should emit events: window_decision(route, tenant, old, new, reason, sample_rate). and a small histogram of observed decode latency vs expected.
kevin: what's the rollout plan? I want canary on dedicated first, then hosted with opt-in flag for a week. if we see regressions auto-revert.
miguel: plan: 1) unit tests + microbenchmark, 2) dry-run telemetry for 24h (no behavior change), 3) canary on staging, 4) dedicated canary, 5) 5% hosted, 6) ramp.
jen: edge case: streaming responses where decode time is front-loaded vs back-loaded. variance metric might misclassify.
miguel: good call. we will compute variance on "time-to-first-N-tokens" and "tail-slope" features instead of single decode time. feature vector kept tiny: (t_first_8, t_first_32, t_total_est).
ops-bot: deploy-bot detected a spike in staging yesterday at 09:12 UTC — flagging that window changes can coincide with autoscaler oscillation.
kevin: exactly — we need to couple window adjustments with a backoff to autoscaler signals. do not increase window when GPU saturation > 80% last 2 minutes.
miguel: agreed, add a gating condition: if node_utilization_high then freeze parameter changes for T_freeze.
jen: API surface: do we expose a minimal admission hint to customers? e.g., "batching_hint": { "preferred_window_ms": 40 } so they can opt-in or pin?
miguel: expose opt-in hints only. we don't want tenants to game the system. internal-only suggest + an enterprise pin for legacy customers.
sara: telemetry details: please include a short dashboard plan in the RFC — routes, tenant top-20 deltas, histogram of request sizes, window tuning events, and annotations for autoscaler.
miguel: will include. also adding a compact trace tag so we can correlate a spike to a window change: tag format: rw.window.v1/<route>/<reason>/<digest>.
oliver: what about preemptive eviction? if a window grows and causes latency slip for low-latency lanes, we need a quick reclaim.
miguel: we already have soft-preempt: mark batches as reclaimable and accelerate their processing with lane prioritization. new piece: evictable batches get a 'drain_timeout' that's smaller.
jen: can you paste pseudo-config for the new tuning knobs?
miguel: ```
# route tuning sample
route: text-gen-2
variance_alpha: 0.2 # EWMA smoothing
window_min_ms: 6
window_max_ms: 120
change_threshold: 0.25 # fractional change needed to apply
stability_windows: 3 # consecutive windows
freeze_on_util_pct: 80
freeze_duration_s: 30
```
kevin: looks sane. please add a safety hard cap on max queueing_ms to avoid unbounded latency.
miguel: added window_max_ms. also we'll enforce SLA-based top-level clamp: if route has latency_slo=100ms, ensure window_max_ms < latency_slo/2 by default.
sara: let's get a short POST-RFC checklist: unit tests, microbench results (median/99/999), telemetry dry-run, canary plan, rollback criteria, doc updates.
miguel: noted. I'll draft RFC v2 with the checklist and the dashboard mockups. any other concerns?
jen: backward compatibility: ensure old admission APIs still work; keep a compatibility flag.
kevin: ensure the change does not affect billing attribution (batch size influence). discuss with billing.
miguel: will sync with billing. thanks all. marking action items in the RFC draft and pinging ops for dashboard. :thumbsup:
